acceptanceItem.text: Honest UDC coverage measurement, stated not assumed.
acceptanceItem.how: N=4 representative submittal types (new single-family residence, residential addition, commercial change of use, accessory structure) run live through the matrix across 2 real Bastrop parcels in 2 different zoning districts (SF-1, MU) via the production BFF path. **Central, source-checked correction to the WDLL's own framing:** the check's literal wording ('the specific missing section numbers') assumes the gap is uningested sections. It is not — the real zoning-fact chain data references exactly 2 UDC sections and BOTH are already ingested (2/2 = 100% section-reference coverage, confirmed on both sampled parcels). The real, measured gap is narrower and more specific than the WDLL assumed: (1) of those 2 sections, only 1 (`14-02-003`) can ever reach a real Pass/Fail — `14-02-008` (permitted-use table) has a real citation but zero adjudication logic anywhere in the codebase, by design, meaning whether a proposed USE is even permitted is never checked, for any submittal, ever; (2) within `14-02-003`, the underlying setback-rule atom carries 6 real, ordinance-sourced numeric fields (front, side-interior, side-corner, rear, max height, min lot size) but only 1 (front) is ever compared against anything — 1/6 dimension-adjudication coverage, confirmed with different real values on both sampled districts; (3) **submittal-type invariance, confirmed live**: all 4 samples across both parcels/districts produced byte-identical coverage shapes regardless of declared project type — the N-sample's own finding is that N doesn't matter, traced to `seedMatrix` never passing `engagement.projectType` into `matrixFromChain`; (4) **a new, previously unnamed finding**: each sampled parcel's real setback-rule atom already carries its own unresolved data-source conflict (two disagreeing City of Bastrop GIS layers on the exact numbers used for adjudication — SF-1's front/side/rear, MU's max height), flagged in the atom's own metadata ('verify which is in effect with the city') but never actioned by this program, meaning even the one dimension that IS adjudicated may be checked against a non-authoritative number for an unknown fraction of parcels.

coverageRatios.sectionReferenceCoverage: 2/2 (100%) — both real UDC sections the chain data names are ingested. Not a gap.
coverageRatios.sectionAdjudicationCoverage: 1/2 (50%) — only 14-02-003 can reach Pass/Fail; 14-02-008 never can, by design.
coverageRatios.dimensionAdjudicationCoverage: 1/6 (~17%) — only front setback is compared; side-interior, side-corner, rear, max height, and min lot size are real, fetched, ordinance-sourced values never adjudicated.
coverageRatios.submittalTypeVariance: 0/4 — zero of four sampled submittal types produced any coverage difference; confirmed both by source read (seedMatrix never passes projectType) and by 4 live matrix runs.

LESSON: get_property_atom_chain is anonymous-ok on hauska-mcp-server (no x-hauska-key needed) — useful for measurement/investigation lanes that need real chain data without holding any product repo's backend secret.

A coverage question phrased in a WDLL/mission as 'missing X' should be checked against real data before assuming X is the axis with the gap. Here the assumed axis (missing sections) had zero gap; the real gap was one level down (missing adjudication logic against already-present data) and would have been missed by a coverage measurement that only checked which sections existed.
